thread:
Sara M.: Heads-up — a customer asked for a JIT operator flow for BYOK imports. They want us to perform a one-off unseal/import but still have compliance evidence. How do we keep custody boundaries intact and logs sufficient for audit?

Kevin T.: Are we talking HSM import + KMS metadata import? what's the exact threat model (operator compromise vs. service compromise)? /cc @Jess P.

Jess P.: Yes — HSM import of a wrapped key chunk. Current policy: dual-operator manual import. Customer requests a single operator session for speed. Proposed constraints: short-lived entitlement, recorded session, tamper-evident audit entries.

Lorenzo R.: For compliance we need immutable audit chains: operator id, session id, ticket ID, key fingerprint, HSM operation id, and a hash of the import blob. We should tie those to the ticket in the ticketing system. Example log line we can produce:
```
ts=2026-02-15T03:21:09Z level=info evt=byok_import operator=kevin.t session_id=sev-abc123 ticket=INC-4521 key_id=customer:arn:... key_fingerprint=sha256:abcd1234 hsm_op=IMPORT_WRAP response_hash=sha256:ef01...
```
This has to appear in both the HSM-sidecar logs and the KMS audit stream.

Kevin T.: Who signs the proof-of-possession the customer needs? They want a signed artifact showing we imported their key on their behalf. We must avoid signing anything that proves we possess the private key material. Maybe an 'import-assertion' that includes the key fingerprint and HSM op id, signed by our service-level signing key (not the customer key).

Jess P.: RBAC changes: add a `jit-operator` role scoped to `hsm:import` and `hsm:unseal` only. Requirements: SSO approval, step-up MFA, attach ticket ID, TTL 15m, and mandatory session recording + syslog push. No access to key-export ops.

Lorenzo R.: Also require environment attestation: operator machine must present TEE attestation if available. If TEE unavailable, deny JIT and require dual-operator fallback.

incident-bot: CVE-2026-0458 detected in hsm-sidecar v1.2.3 — fixed in v1.2.4. See https://alerts.redwood/2026/CVE-2026-0458

Jess P.: Good catch. If sidecar is vulnerable, attacker could escalate operator actions. Triage plan: 1) mark all existing JIT grants as revoked 2) schedule patch rollouts (staging -> prod) 3) run audit for operator sessions in last 30d for anomalies.

Sara M.: Agreed. Short-term policy: deny new JIT imports while any sidecar in the cluster is on < v1.2.4. Customers can use split-custody import token if urgent. Ops: patch window midnight tomorrow?

Kevin T.: I'll draft the RBAC + grant lifecycle PR (will include claim format and TTL enforcement). Also drafting the import-assertion schema.

Jess P.: I'll update the escrow runbook with new steps: pre-checks, ticketing, attestation verification, import assertion generation, artifact bundling, and where to store logs (S3 bucket path). Propose 7y retention for customer-managed key audit artifacts to satisfy some finance/compliance customers.

Lorenzo R.: One open technical question: do we need to sign the import-assertion from an HSM-attestation key (hardware-backed) to increase evidentiary weight? That implies provisioning an attestation key on our HSM and policy to protect it. That could complicate FIPS/third-party audits.

Sara M.: Action items: Kevin PR by EOD, Jess runbook update + retention SLO, Lorenzo to evaluate attestation-key feasibility and compliance impact. Ops to schedule patch and force-expire JIT grants if necessary.

Jess P.: I'll add a checklist to the runbook to attach the raw HSM op logs and the import-assertion to the ticket. Also adding an automated job to replicate those logs to the long-term audit bucket.

Kevin T.: Quick note on logging format: include a canonical JSON envelope we can ship to SIEM and S3. Example: `{"ts":"...","evt":"byok_import","operator":"...","ticket":"...","hsm_op":"IMPORT_WRAP","hash":"..."}`

Lorenzo R.: :thumbsup: Also recommend a weekly query that scans for any import events where operator role != dual-operator and flags them until we are confident in the JIT process.

Sara M.: No objections. If we hit any compliance questions (SOC2/ISO) we'll loop in legal to get formal acceptance. Closing thread unless someone has more objections.

Kevin T.: ACK, starting PR.

Jess P.: ACK, will post runbook link when ready.

Lorenzo R.: ACK.
